## Determination — Packet P6J-14

**Governing:** CIP-010-4 R2 Part 2.1
**Premise applied:** This Part carries two conjunct duties — (a) monitor for baseline-configuration changes at least once every 35 calendar days, and (b) document and investigate detected unauthorized changes.

### Duty (a): Monitor ≤ 35 days — SATISFIED
The candidate states a file integrity monitoring agent on each in-scope BES Cyber System reports configuration drift to the OT Security dashboard every 24 hours. A 24-hour reporting cadence is strictly more frequent than the minimum once-every-35-calendar-days floor, and it applies to each in-scope BES Cyber System. This duty is met on the evidence shown, subject to SME review that "configuration drift" reporting maps to changes in the R1 Part 1.1 baseline configuration (i.e., that drift is measured against a documented baseline, not merely prior-state deltas).

### Duty (b): Document and investigate detected unauthorized changes — NOT ADDRESSED
The candidate describes only detection and reporting. It contains no language requiring that detected unauthorized changes be documented or investigated, nor any assignment of who investigates, by when, or what record is produced. Because the premise states both duties are conjunctive (both required), a candidate that satisfies only duty (a) cannot satisfy the Part as a whole.

### Coverage
**Partial.** The candidate covers duty (a) and is missing the entire "document and investigate detected unauthorized changes" obligation of duty (b).

### Evidence an auditor would look for
- For (a): FIM agent inventory mapped to in-scope BES Cyber Systems; dashboard/alert logs showing ≤35-day (here 24-hour) coverage; the documented baseline configuration per R1 Part 1.1 that drift is measured against.
- For (b): change-investigation records, documented findings of unauthorized changes, and evidence of remediation/disposition — none of which the candidate language generates.

### Cross-References
CIP-010-4 R2 Part 1.1

### Duty (a): Monitor ≤ 35 days — SATISFIED

A 24-hour reporting cadence is strictly more frequent than the minimum once-every-35-calendar-days floor, and it applies to each in-scope BES Cyber System. This duty is met on the evidence shown, subject to SME review that "configuration drift" reporting maps to changes in the R1 Part 1.1 baseline configuration (i.e., that drift is measured against a documented baseline, not merely prior-state deltas).

### Duty (b): Document and investigate detected unauthorized changes — NOT ADDRESSED
The candidate describes only detection and reporting. It contains no language requiring that detected unauthorized changes be documented or investigated, nor any assignment of who investigates, by when, or what record is produced. Because the premise states both duties are conjunctive (both required), a candidate that satisfies only duty (a) cannot satisfy the Part as a whole.

### Coverage
**Partial.** The candidate covers duty (a) and is missing the entire "document and investigate detected unauthorized changes" obligation of duty (b).

### Evidence an auditor would look for
- For (a): FIM agent inventory mapped to in-scope BES Cyber Systems; dashboard/alert logs showing ≤35-day (here 24-hour) coverage; the documented baseline configuration per R1 Part 1.1 that drift is measured against.
- For (b): change-investigation records, documented findings of unauthorized changes, and evidence of remediation/disposition — none of which the candidate language generates.

### Cross-References
CIP-010-4 R2 Part 1.1 (baseline configuration definition); CIP-010-4 R3/R5 (event response and reporting, if unauthorized changes escalate to security events).

**Bottom line:** The candidate text is a detection-only control. It satisfies the monitoring-frequency conjunct but omits the document-and-investigate conjunct, so it does not fully satisfy CIP-010-4 R2 Part 2.1 as stated in the governing text and premises.
